+"""Module location.

+

+Secret: how an imported module name is found — first as a source file or

+package in the project directory, otherwise by importing an installed module

+at runtime (with its side effects contained).

+"""

+

+import contextlib

+import importlib

+import io

+import os

+import sys

+

+SOURCE = "source"

+RUNTIME = "runtime"

+DIRECTORY = "directory"

+

+

+class Located:

+    """Where a module lives: a source file, a bare directory, or a live module."""

+

+    def __init__(self, how, path=None, module=None):

+        self.how = how

+        self.path = path

+        self.module = module

+

+

+class ModuleLocator:

+    def __init__(self, project_dir):

+        self._project_dir = os.path.abspath(project_dir)

+        self._runtime_cache = {}

+

+    def locate(self, dotted, level=0, importer_path=None):

+        """Locate ``dotted`` (relative to ``importer_path`` when ``level`` > 0)."""

+        parts = [p for p in dotted.split(".") if p] if dotted else []

+        if level > 0:

+            base = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(importer_path or self._project_dir))

+            for _ in range(level - 1):

+                base = os.path.dirname(base)

+            return self._locate_in(base, parts)

+        if not parts:

+            return None

+        roots = [self._project_dir]

+        if importer_path:

+            own = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(importer_path))

+            if own not in roots:

+                roots.append(own)

+        namespace = None

+        for root in roots:

+            found = self._locate_in(root, parts)

+            if found is not None and found.how == SOURCE:

+                return found

+            namespace = namespace or found

+        module = self._import_runtime(".".join(parts))

+        if module is not None:

+            return Located(RUNTIME, module=module)

+        return namespace

+

+    def locate_in_directory(self, directory, name):

+        """Locate submodule ``name`` of the package stored in ``directory``."""

+        return self._locate_in(directory, [name])

+

+    def _locate_in(self, base, parts):

+        path = base

+        for index, part in enumerate(parts):

+            last = index == len(parts) - 1

+            package = os.path.join(path, part)

+            if os.path.isdir(package):

+                if last:

+                    return self._package(package)

+                path = package

+                continue

+            if last and os.path.isfile(package + ".py"):

+                return Located(SOURCE, path=package + ".py")

+            return None

+        return self._package(path)

+

+    @staticmethod

+    def _package(directory):

+        init = os.path.join(directory, "__init__.py")

+        if os.path.isfile(init):

+            return Located(SOURCE, path=init)

+        return Located(DIRECTORY, path=directory)

+

+    def _import_runtime(self, name):

+        if name in self._runtime_cache:

+            return self._runtime_cache[name]

+        module = None

+        saved_path = list(sys.path)

+        sys.path[:] = [p for p in sys.path

+                       if p and os.path.abspath(p) not in (self._project_dir, _TOOL_DIR)]

+        try:

+            with _silenced_descriptors(), contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()), \

+                    contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):

+                module = importlib.import_module(name)

+        except BaseException:  # noqa: B902 - arbitrary import code may do anything

+            module = None

+        finally:

+            sys.path[:] = saved_path

+        self._runtime_cache[name] = module

+        return module

+

+

+@contextlib.contextmanager

+def _silenced_descriptors():

+    """Route OS-level stdout/stderr to the null device (for C extensions)."""

+    saved = []

+    try:

+        sys.stdout.flush()

+        sys.stderr.flush()

+        devnull = os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY)

+        for fd in (1, 2):

+            saved.append((fd, os.dup(fd)))

+            os.dup2(devnull, fd)

+        os.close(devnull)

+    except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError):

+        pass

+    try:

+        yield

+    finally:

+        for fd, copy in saved:

+            os.dup2(copy, fd)

+            os.close(copy)

+

+

+_TOOL_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

+"""Error-tolerant parsing.

+

+Secret: the repair strategy used to turn syntactically broken source into a

+syntax tree. Lines keep their numbers, so positions in the returned tree

+match positions in the original text.

+"""

+

+import ast

+import keyword

+import re

+

+_ORIGINAL, _PASSED, _BLANKED = 0, 1, 2

+_HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"on line (\d+)")

+_DEF_RE = re.compile(r"^(\s*)(async\s+)?def\s+([^\W\d]\w*)")

+_CLASS_RE = re.compile(r"^(\s*)class\s+([^\W\d]\w*)")

+_PARAM_RE = re.compile(r"\s*\*{0,2}\s*([^\W\d]\w*)")

+_SALVAGED = 3

+

+

+def parse_tolerant(text):

+    """Return an ``ast.Module`` for ``text``, repairing errors as needed."""

+    lines = text.replace("\0", " ").split("\n")

+    state = [_ORIGINAL] * len(lines)

+    patched_headers = set()

+    for _ in range(4 * len(lines) + 20):

+        try:

+            return ast.parse("\n".join(lines))

+        except SyntaxError as exc:

+            if not _repair(lines, state, patched_headers, exc):

+                break

+        except (ValueError, RecursionError, MemoryError):

+            break

+    return ast.Module(body=[], type_ignores=[])

+

+

+def _repair(lines, state, patched_headers, exc):

+    msg = exc.msg or ""

+    if msg.startswith("expected an indented block"):

+        match = _HEADER_RE.search(msg)

+        if match:

+            header = int(match.group(1)) - 1

+            if 0 <= header < len(lines) and header not in patched_headers:

+                patched_headers.add(header)

+                lines[header] = _with_pass_body(lines[header])

+                return True

+    idx = (exc.lineno or len(lines)) - 1

+    idx = max(0, min(idx, len(lines) - 1))

+    if msg.startswith("unterminated triple-quoted string") and ("eof", idx) not in patched_headers:

+        patched_headers.add(("eof", idx))

+        text = lines[idx][max(0, (exc.offset or 1) - 1):]

+        quotes = [q for q in ('"""', "'''") if q in text]

+        if quotes:

+            lines[-1] += min(quotes, key=text.index)

+            return True

+    while idx >= 0 and (state[idx] == _BLANKED or not lines[idx].strip()):

+        idx -= 1

+    if idx < 0:

+        return False

+    if msg.startswith("expected 'except' or 'finally' block"):

+        header = _find_try_header(lines, idx)

+        if header is not None:

+            lines[header] = lines[header][: _indent_width(lines[header])] + "if True:"

+            return True

+    if msg.startswith("unexpected indent"):

+        _blank_block(lines, state, idx)

+        return True

+    if state[idx] == _ORIGINAL and lines[idx].rstrip().endswith(":"):

+        salvaged = _salvage_header(lines[idx])

+        if salvaged is not None and salvaged != lines[idx]:

+            state[idx] = _SALVAGED

+            lines[idx] = salvaged

+            return True

+    if state[idx] in (_ORIGINAL, _SALVAGED):

+        stripped = lines[idx].lstrip()

+        indent = lines[idx][: len(lines[idx]) - len(stripped)]

+        state[idx] = _PASSED

+        lines[idx] = indent + "pass"

+    else:

+        state[idx] = _BLANKED

+        lines[idx] = ""

+    return True

+

+

+def _blank_block(lines, state, idx):

+    """Blank an orphaned indented block: line ``idx`` and deeper/equal lines after it."""

+    width = _indent_width(lines[idx])

+    end = idx

+    while end < len(lines) and (not lines[end].strip() or _indent_width(lines[end]) >= width):

+        if lines[end].strip():

+            state[end] = _BLANKED

+            lines[end] = ""

+        end += 1

+

+

+def _find_try_header(lines, idx):

+    """The ``try:`` line whose handlers are missing at line ``idx``."""

+    limit = _indent_width(lines[idx]) if lines[idx].strip() else None

+    for number in range(min(idx, len(lines) - 1), -1, -1):

+        stripped = lines[number].strip()

+        if not stripped:

+            continue

+        width = _indent_width(lines[number])

+        if stripped.replace(" ", "") == "try:" and (limit is None or width <= limit):

+            return number

+        if limit is not None and width < limit:

+            return None

+    return None

+

+

+def _indent_width(line):

+    return len(line) - len(line.lstrip())

+

+

+def _salvage_header(line):

+    """Reduce a broken ``def``/``class`` header to a minimal valid one."""

+    match = _DEF_RE.match(line)

+    if match:

+        params = []

+        rest = line[match.end():]

+        if rest.lstrip().startswith("("):

+            inside = rest[rest.index("(") + 1: rest.rfind(":")]

+            for piece in inside.split(","):

+                found = _PARAM_RE.match(piece)

+                if found and found.group(1) not in params \

+                        and not keyword.iskeyword(found.group(1)):

+                    params.append(found.group(1))

+        return "%s%sdef %s(%s):" % (match.group(1), match.group(2) or "", match.group(3),

+                                    ", ".join(params))

+    match = _CLASS_RE.match(line)

+    if match:

+        return "%sclass %s:" % (match.group(1), match.group(2))

+    return None

+

+

+def _with_pass_body(line):

+    """Give a block header such as ``if x:`` an inline ``pass`` body."""

+    stripped = line.rstrip()

+    if stripped.endswith(":"):

+        return stripped + " pass"

+    colon = stripped.rfind(":")

+    if colon >= 0:

+        return stripped[: colon + 1] + " pass"

+    return stripped

+"""Cursor context detection.

+

+Secret: how the text before the cursor is lexed to decide whether a bare

+name, an attribute, or nothing is being completed, what prefix has been

+typed, and which source text forms the receiver of an attribute access.

+"""

+

+NAME = "name"

+ATTRIBUTE = "attribute"

+NONE = "none"

+

+_CLOSERS = {")": "(", "]": "[", "}": "{"}

+_STRING_PREFIX_CHARS = set("rRbBuUfF")

+

+

+class CursorContext:

+    def __init__(self, kind, prefix="", receiver=None):

+        self.kind = kind

+        self.prefix = prefix

+        self.receiver = receiver

+

+

+def analyze(text_before):

+    """Classify the cursor at the end of ``text_before``."""

+    if _inside_string_or_comment(text_before):

+        return CursorContext(NONE)

+    end = len(text_before)

+    start = end

+    while start > 0 and _is_ident_char(text_before[start - 1]):

+        start -= 1

+    prefix = text_before[start:end]

+    if prefix and prefix[0].isdigit():

+        return CursorContext(NONE)

+    pos = _skip_space_back(text_before, start)

+    if pos > 0 and text_before[pos - 1] == ".":

+        dot = pos - 1

+        receiver = _receiver_before(text_before, dot)

+        if receiver is None:

+            return CursorContext(NONE)

+        return CursorContext(ATTRIBUTE, prefix, receiver)

+    return CursorContext(NAME, prefix)

+

+

+def _is_ident_char(ch):

+    return ch == "_" or ch.isalnum()

+

+

+def _skip_space_back(text, pos):

+    while pos > 0 and text[pos - 1] in " \t":

+        pos -= 1

+    return pos

+

+

+def _inside_string_or_comment(text):

+    i, n = 0, len(text)

+    while i < n:

+        ch = text[i]

+        if ch == "#":

+            newline = text.find("\n", i)

+            if newline < 0:

+                return True

+            i = newline + 1

+        elif ch in "'\"":

+            quote = text[i : i + 3] if text[i : i + 3] in ("'''", '"""') else ch

+            i += len(quote)

+            closed = False

+            while i < n:

+                if text[i] == "\\":

+                    i += 2

+                    continue

+                if text.startswith(quote, i):

+                    i += len(quote)

+                    closed = True

+                    break

+                if text[i] == "\n" and len(quote) == 1:

+                    break

+                i += 1

+            if not closed and i >= n:

+                return True

+        else:

+            i += 1

+    return False

+

+

+def _receiver_before(text, dot):

+    """Source text of the primary expression ending just before ``dot``."""

+    if dot > 0 and text[dot - 1] == ".":

+        return None

+    pos = _skip_space_back(text, dot)

+    begin = _scan_primary(text, pos)

+    if begin is None or begin == pos:

+        return None

+    receiver = text[begin:pos].strip()

+    if receiver and (receiver[0].isdigit() and receiver.replace("_", "").isdigit()):

+        return None

+    return receiver

+

+

+def _scan_primary(text, pos):

+    """Scan one primary (atom plus trailers) backwards; return its start."""

+    while True:

+        if pos == 0:

+            return None

+        ch = text[pos - 1]

+        if ch in _CLOSERS:

+            opener = _match_open(text, pos - 1)

+            if opener is None:

+                return None

+            pos = opener

+            if pos > 0 and (_is_ident_char(text[pos - 1]) or text[pos - 1] in _CLOSERS

+                            or text[pos - 1] in "'\""):

+                continue

+            return _after_dot_chain(text, pos)

+        if ch in "'\"":

+            start = _match_string_start(text, pos)

+            if start is None:

+                return None

+            return start

+        if _is_ident_char(ch):

+            while pos > 0 and _is_ident_char(text[pos - 1]):

+                pos -= 1

+            return _after_dot_chain(text, pos)

+        return None

+

+

+def _after_dot_chain(text, pos):

+    """If the atom starting at ``pos`` is preceded by a dot, keep scanning."""

+    before = _skip_space_back(text, pos)

+    if before > 0 and text[before - 1] == "." and not (before > 1 and text[before - 2] == "."):

+        inner = _scan_primary(text, _skip_space_back(text, before - 1))

+        return inner if inner is not None else pos

+    return pos

+

+

+def _match_open(text, close_index):

+    depth = 0

+    i = close_index

+    while i >= 0:

+        ch = text[i]

+        if ch in "'\"":

+            start = _match_string_start(text, i + 1)

+            if start is None:

+                return None

+            i = start - 1

+            continue

+        if ch in _CLOSERS:

+            depth += 1

+        elif ch in "([{":

+            depth -= 1

+            if depth == 0:

+                return i

+        i -= 1

+    return None

+

+

+def _match_string_start(text, end):

+    """Given ``text[end - 1]`` is a closing quote, find the literal's start."""

+    quote_char = text[end - 1]

+    triple = quote_char * 3

+    if end >= 3 and text[end - 3 : end] == triple:

+        found = text.rfind(triple, 0, end - 3)

+        start = found if found >= 0 else None

+    else:

+        i = end - 2

+        start = None

+        while i >= 0:

+            if text[i] == quote_char and not _escaped(text, i):

+                start = i

+                break

+            if text[i] == "\n":

+                break

+            i -= 1

+    if start is None:

+        return None

+    head = start

+    while head > 0 and start - head < 2 and text[head - 1] in _STRING_PREFIX_CHARS:

+        head -= 1

+    if head < start and not (head > 0 and _is_ident_char(text[head - 1])):

+        return head

+    return start

+

+

+def _escaped(text, i):

+    count = 0

+    while i - 1 - count >= 0 and text[i - 1 - count] == "\\":

+        count += 1

+    return count % 2 == 1

--- sithlib/inference.py
+++ sithlib/inference.py
@@ -0,0 +1,630 @@
+"""Static inference.

+

+Secret: how bindings and expressions are mapped to values (modules, classes,

+functions, instances), how names are resolved through scopes, star imports

+and builtins, and how the members of a value are enumerated.

+

+Clients see three abstractions:

+  * ``Project``  - opens the main file and returns a ``Location`` for a cursor.

+  * ``Value``    - has ``kind``, ``type_name`` and ``members()``.

+  * ``Entity``   - a named member/visible name with ``presentation()`` giving

+                   ``(kind, type_name)`` and ``value()`` giving a ``Value``.

+"""

+

+import ast

+import os

+import types

+

+from . import introspect, scopes, vocabulary

+from .modules import DIRECTORY, RUNTIME, SOURCE, ModuleLocator

+

+MODULE = "module"

+CLASS = "class"

+FUNCTION = "function"

+INSTANCE = "instance"

+PARAM = "param"

+STATEMENT = "statement"

+UNKNOWN = "unknown"

+

+_LITERAL_TYPES = {

+    ast.JoinedStr: str,

+    ast.List: list, ast.ListComp: list,

+    ast.Tuple: tuple,

+    ast.Dict: dict, ast.DictComp: dict,

+    ast.Set: set, ast.SetComp: set,

+    ast.GeneratorExp: types.GeneratorType,

+    ast.Compare: bool,

+}

+_ARITHMETIC_TYPES = (int, float, complex, str, bytes, list, tuple)

+

+

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+# Values

+

+class Value:

+    kind = UNKNOWN

+    type_name = None

+

+    def members(self):

+        return {}

+

+    def attribute(self, name):

+        entity = self.members().get(name)

+        return entity.value() if entity is not None else UNKNOWN_VALUE

+

+    def call(self):

+        return UNKNOWN_VALUE

+

+    def instantiate(self):

+        return UNKNOWN_VALUE

+

+    def builtin_type(self):

+        """For instances of builtin types, the type object; else None."""

+        return None

+

+

+UNKNOWN_VALUE = Value()

+

+

+class RuntimeValue(Value):

+    """A live object obtained by importing a module."""

+

+    def __init__(self, project, obj):

+        self._project = project

+        self._obj = obj

+        self.kind = introspect.kind_of(obj)

+        if self.kind == INSTANCE:

+            self.type_name = introspect.type_name(obj)

+

+    def members(self):

+        return {name: RuntimeEntity(self._project, name, self._obj)

+                for name in introspect.attribute_names(self._obj)}

+

+    def attribute(self, name):

+        ok, value = introspect.get_attribute(self._obj, name)

+        if ok:

+            return RuntimeValue(self._project, value)

+        if self.kind == MODULE:

+            module_name = getattr(self._obj, "__name__", None)

+            if module_name:

+                found = self._project.module_value(module_name + "." + name)

+                if found is not None:

+                    return found

+        return UNKNOWN_VALUE

+

+    def call(self):

+        return self.instantiate()

+

+    def instantiate(self):

+        if self.kind == CLASS:

+            return RuntimeInstance(self._project, self._obj)

+        return UNKNOWN_VALUE

+

+    def builtin_type(self):

+        return type(self._obj) if self.kind == INSTANCE else None

+

+

+class RuntimeInstance(Value):

+    """An instance of a runtime class, known only by its class."""

+

+    kind = INSTANCE

+

+    def __init__(self, project, cls):

+        self._project = project

+        self._cls = cls

+        self._sample = introspect.sample_instance(cls)

+        self.type_name = introspect.class_name(cls)

+

+    def members(self):

+        return {name: RuntimeEntity(self._project, name, self._sample, from_class=self._cls)

+                for name in introspect.attribute_names(self._cls)}

+

+    def attribute(self, name):

+        return RuntimeEntity(self._project, name, self._sample, from_class=self._cls).value()

+

+    def builtin_type(self):

+        return self._cls

+

+

+class UnresolvedModule(Value):

+    kind = MODULE

+

+

+class DirectoryModule(Value):

+    """A package directory without ``__init__.py``."""

+

+    kind = MODULE

+

+    def __init__(self, project, directory):

+        self._project = project

+        self._directory = directory

+

+    def attribute(self, name):

+        found = self._project.submodule_value(self._directory, name)

+        return found if found is not None else UNKNOWN_VALUE

+

+

+class StaticModule(Value):

+    kind = MODULE

+

+    def __init__(self, analysis):

+        self._analysis = analysis

+

+    def members(self):

+        return self._analysis.module_members()

+

+    def attribute(self, name):

+        entity = self.members().get(name)

+        if entity is not None:

+            return entity.value()

+        package_dir = self._analysis.package_dir()

+        if package_dir:

+            found = self._analysis.project.submodule_value(package_dir, name)

+            if found is not None:

+                return found

+        return UNKNOWN_VALUE

+

+

+class StaticFunction(Value):

+    kind = FUNCTION

+

+    def __init__(self, analysis, scope):

+        self._analysis = analysis

+        self._scope = scope

+

+    def call(self):

+        if self._scope.is_async():

+            return UNKNOWN_VALUE

+        project = self._analysis.project

+        key = ("call", id(self._scope))

+        if not project.enter(key):

+            return UNKNOWN_VALUE

+        try:

+            view = _View(scope=self._scope, order=float("inf"))

+            for expr in self._scope.returned_expressions():

+                value = self._analysis.evaluate(expr, self._scope, view)

+                if value.kind != UNKNOWN:

+                    return value

+            return UNKNOWN_VALUE

+        finally:

+            project.leave(key)

+

+

+class StaticClass(Value):

+    kind = CLASS

+

+    def __init__(self, analysis, scope):

+        self._analysis = analysis

+        self._scope = scope

+        self.name = scope.name

+

+    def identity(self):

+        return id(self._scope)

+

+    def bases(self):

+        project = self._analysis.project

+        key = ("bases", id(self._scope))

+        if not project.enter(key):

+            return []

+        try:

+            parent = self._scope.parent

+            view = _View()

+            result = []

+            for expr in self._scope.base_expressions():

+                value = self._analysis.evaluate(expr, parent, view)

+                if isinstance(value, StaticClass) and value.identity() != self.identity():

+                    result.append(value)

+            return result

+        finally:

+            project.leave(key)

+

+    def mro(self):

+        return _linearize(self, set())

+

+    def members(self):

+        result = {}

+        for cls in reversed(self.mro()):

+            for event in cls._scope.all_events():

+                if event.name and event.form != scopes.STAR:

+                    result[event.name] = BindingEntity(cls._analysis, event)

+        return result

+

+    def instance_members(self):

+        result = self.members()

+        for cls in reversed(self.mro()):

+            for event in cls._scope.instance_attribute_events():

+                result[event.name] = BindingEntity(cls._analysis, event)

+        return result

+

+    def call(self):

+        return self.instantiate()

+

+    def instantiate(self):

+        return StaticInstance(self)

+

+

+class StaticInstance(Value):

+    kind = INSTANCE

+

+    def __init__(self, cls):

+        self._cls = cls

+        self.type_name = cls.name

+

+    def members(self):

+        return self._cls.instance_members()

+

+

+def _linearize(cls, seen):

+    """C3 linearization of statically known classes (DFS on conflict)."""

+    if cls.identity() in seen:

+        return [cls]

+    seen = seen | {cls.identity()}

+    bases = cls.bases()

+    sequences = [_linearize(base, seen) for base in bases] + [list(bases)]

+    result = [cls]

+    sequences = [list(s) for s in sequences if s]

+    while sequences:

+        for sequence in sequences:

+            head = sequence[0]

+            if not any(head.identity() in [c.identity() for c in s[1:]] for s in sequences):

+                break

+        else:

+            for sequence in sequences:

+                for item in sequence:

+                    if item.identity() not in [c.identity() for c in result]:

+                        result.append(item)

+            return result

+        result.append(head)

+        sequences = [[c for c in s if c.identity() != head.identity()] for s in sequences]

+        sequences = [s for s in sequences if s]

+    return result

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+class RuntimeEntity(Entity):

+            return introspect.get_attribute(self._owner, self.name)

+        if ok and introspect.is_data_descriptor(obj):

+            return False, None

+        return ok, obj

+

+        return (kind, None)

+    def value(self):

+            try:

+    # -- bindings --------------------------------------------------------

+            return RuntimeInstance(self.project, dict)

+            annotated = self.evaluate(details["annotation"], function.parent, _View())

+        return UNKNOWN_VALUE

+    def _import_from_value(self, details):

+        module_name, level, attr = details["module"], details["level"], details["attr"]

+        if module is not None:

+            value = module.attribute(attr)

+            return self.evaluate(node.value, scope, view).attribute(node.attr)

+            return self.evaluate(node.func, scope, view).call()

+            return self.evaluate(node.operand, scope, view)

+                    and left_type in _ARITHMETIC_TYPES:

+                return left

+        return UNKNOWN_VALUE

+def _unpack(expr, path):

+    for index in path:

+        if not isinstance(expr, (ast.Tuple, ast.List)):

+            return None

+        if any(isinstance(e, ast.Starred) for e in expr.elts) or index >= len(expr.elts):

+            return None

+        expr = expr.elts[index]

+    return expr

+

+

+class Location:

+    """A cursor position inside the main file."""

+

+    def __init__(self, analysis, scope, line):

+        self._analysis = analysis

+        self._scope = scope

+        self._view = _View(line=line)

+

+    def visible_entities(self):

+        return self._analysis.visible(self._scope, self._view)

+

+    def evaluate(self, expression_text):

+        try:

+            node = ast.parse(expression_text.strip(), mode="eval").body

+        except (SyntaxError, ValueError, RecursionError, MemoryError):

+            return UNKNOWN_VALUE

+        return self._analysis.evaluate(node, self._scope, self._view)

+

+

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+# Project

+

+class Project:

+    def __init__(self, main_path, main_text):

+        self._main_path = os.path.abspath(main_path)

+        self._locator = ModuleLocator(os.path.dirname(self._main_path))

+        self._analyses = {}

+        self._active = set()

+        self.main = Analysis(self, self._main_path, main_text)

+        self._analyses[self._main_path] = self.main

+

+    def enter(self, key):

+        if key in self._active:

+            return False

+        self._active.add(key)

+        return True

+

+    def leave(self, key):

+        self._active.discard(key)

+

+    def location(self, line, col):

+        return self.main.location(line, col)

+

+    def module_value(self, dotted, level=0, importer_path=None):

+        located = self._locator.locate(dotted, level, importer_path or self._main_path)

+        return self._wrap(located)

+

+    def submodule_value(self, directory, name):

+        return self._wrap(self._locator.locate_in_directory(directory, name))

+

+    def _wrap(self, located):

+        if located is None:

+            return None

+        if located.how == RUNTIME:

+            return RuntimeValue(self, located.module)

+        if located.how == DIRECTORY:

+            return DirectoryModule(self, located.path)

+        if located.how == SOURCE:

+            return StaticModule(self._analysis_for(located.path))

+        return None

+

+    def _analysis_for(self, path):

+        path = os.path.abspath(path)

+        if path not in self._analyses:

+            try:

+                with open(path, "rb") as handle:

+                    text = handle.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

+            except OSError:

+                text = ""

+            self._analyses[path] = Analysis(self, path, text)

+        return self._analyses[path]

+                       annotation=arg.annotation, star="")

+            index += 1

+        if args.kwarg:

+            child_bind(child, args.kwarg.arg, node.lineno, function=child, index=index,

+                       annotation=None, star="**")

+        collector = _Collector(child)

+        for statement in _walk_own(node.body):

+            if isinstance(statement, ast.Global):

+                child.globals_declared.update(statement.names)

+        collector.visit_body(node.body)

+        parent_class = child.class_scope()

+        if parent_class is not None and node.name == "__init__" and positional:

+            self_name = positional[0].arg

+            _collect_instance_attributes(parent_class, child, node.body, self_name)

+

+    visit_FunctionDef = _visit_function

+    visit_AsyncFunctionDef = _visit_function

+

+    def visit_ClassDef(self, node):

+        for deco in node.decorator_list:

+            self.visit(deco)

+        for base in node.bases:

+            self.visit(base)

+        self.bind(node.name, CLASS, node.lineno, node=node)

+        child = Scope(Scope.CLASS, node, self.scope, self.scope.tree)

+        self.scope.children.append(child)

+        _Collector(child).visit_body(node.body)

+

+    def visit_Lambda(self, node):

+        pass

+

+    def _visit_comprehension(self, node):

+        for generator in node.generators:

+            self.visit(generator.iter)

+            break

+

+    visit_ListComp = _visit_comprehension

+    visit_SetComp = _visit_comprehension

+    visit_DictComp = _visit_comprehension

+    visit_GeneratorExp = _visit_comprehension

+

+    # -- statements ------------------------------------------------------

+    def visit_Global(self, node):

+        self.scope.globals_declared.update(node.names)

+

+    def visit_Assign(self, node):

+        self.visit(node.value)

+        for target in node.targets:

+            self.bind_target(target, node.lineno, node.value)

+

+    def visit_AnnAssign(self, node):

+        if node.value is not None:

+            self.visit(node.value)

+        if isinstance(node.target, ast.Name):

+            self.bind(node.target.id, ASSIGN, node.lineno, value=node.value, path=(),

+                      annotation=node.annotation)

+        else:

+            self.visit(node.target)

+

+    def visit_AugAssign(self, node):

+        self.visit(node.value)

+        if isinstance(node.target, ast.Name):

+            name = node.target.id

+            scope = self._target_scope(name)

+            if not any(e.name == name for e in scope.events):

+                self.bind(name, OTHER, node.lineno)

+

+    def visit_NamedExpr(self, node):

+        self.visit(node.value)

+        if isinstance(node.target, ast.Name):

+            self.bind(node.target.id, ASSIGN, node.lineno, value=node.value, path=(),

+                      annotation=None)

+

+    def _visit_for(self, node):

+        self.visit(node.iter)

+        self.bind_plain(node.target, node.lineno)

+        self.visit_body(node.body)

+        self.visit_body(node.orelse)

+

+    visit_For = _visit_for

+    visit_AsyncFor = _visit_for

+

+    def _visit_with(self, node):

+        for item in node.items:

+            self.visit(item.context_expr)

+            if item.optional_vars is not None:

+                self.bind_plain(item.optional_vars, node.lineno)

+        self.visit_body(node.body)

+

+    visit_With = _visit_with

+    visit_AsyncWith = _visit_with

+

+    def visit_ExceptHandler(self, node):

+        if node.type is not None:

+            self.visit(node.type)

+        if node.name:

+            self.bind(node.name, EXCEPT, node.lineno, type_expr=node.type)

+        self.visit_body(node.body)

+

+    def visit_Import(self, node):

+        for alias in node.names:

+            if alias.asname:

+                self.bind(alias.asname, IMPORT, node.lineno, module=alias.name, as_name=True)

+            else:

+                first = alias.name.split(".")[0]

+                self.bind(first, IMPORT, node.lineno, module=first, as_name=False)

+

+    def visit_ImportFrom(self, node):

+        module = node.module or ""

+        for alias in node.names:

+            if alias.name == "*":

+                self.bind(None, STAR, node.lineno, module=module, level=node.level)

+            else:

+                self.bind(alias.asname or alias.name, IMPORT_FROM, node.lineno,

+                          module=module, level=node.level, attr=alias.name)

+

+    def visit_MatchAs(self, node):

+        if node.pattern is not None:

+            self.visit(node.pattern)

+        if node.name:

+            self.bind(node.name, OTHER, node.lineno)

+

+    def visit_MatchStar(self, node):

+        if node.name:

+            self.bind(node.name, OTHER, node.lineno)

+

+    def visit_MatchMapping(self, node):

+        self.generic_visit(node)

+        if node.rest:

+            self.bind(node.rest, OTHER, node.lineno)

+

+    def visit_TypeAlias(self, node):

+        if isinstance(node.name, ast.Name):

+            self.bind(node.name.id, OTHER, node.lineno)

+

+

+def child_bind(scope, name, line, **details):

+    scope.events.append(Binding(name, PARAM, line, _Counter.next(), scope, **details))

+

+

+def _collect_instance_attributes(class_scope, init_scope, body, self_name):

+    def is_self_attr(target):

+        return (isinstance(target, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(target.value, ast.Name)

+                and target.value.id == self_name)

+

+    def record(target, line, value, path, annotation=None):

+        if is_self_attr(target):

+            class_scope.instance_events.append(Binding(

+                target.attr, ASSIGN, line, _Counter.next(), init_scope,

+                value=value, path=path, annotation=annotation))

+        elif isinstance(target, (ast.Tuple, ast.List)):

+            for index, element in enumerate(target.elts):

+                record(element, line, value, path + (index,))

+        elif isinstance(target, ast.Starred):

+            record(target.value, line, None, ())

+

+    for node in _walk_own(body):

+        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):

+            for target in node.targets:

+                record(target, node.lineno, node.value, ())

+        elif isinstance(node, ast.AnnAssign):

+            record(node.target, node.lineno, node.value, (), node.annotation)

+        elif isinstance(node, ast.AugAssign) and is_self_attr(node.target):

+            if not any(e.name == node.target.attr for e in class_scope.instance_events):

+                class_scope.instance_events.append(Binding(

+                    node.target.attr, OTHER, node.lineno, _Counter.next(), init_scope))

+"""Source file access.

+

+Secret: how a file on disk is read, decoded and split into lines, and how a

+(1-based line, 0-based column) cursor is validated against it.

+"""

+

+import os

+

+

+class SourceError(Exception):

+    """The file cannot be used as input (missing, undecodable, bad cursor)."""

+

+

+class SourceFile:

+    def __init__(self, path):

+        if not os.path.isfile(path):

+            raise SourceError("not a regular file: %s" % path)

+        try:

+            with open(path, "rb") as handle:

+                raw = handle.read()

+        except OSError as exc:

+            raise SourceError("cannot read %s: %s" % (path, exc))

+        try:

+            text = raw.decode("utf-8")

+        except UnicodeDecodeError:

+            raise SourceError("file is not valid UTF-8: %s" % path)

+        if text.startswith("\ufeff"):

+            text = text[1:]

+        text = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")

+        self._path = os.path.abspath(path)

+        self._lines = text.split("\n")

+

+    @property

+    def path(self):

+        return self._path

+

+    def text(self):

+        return "\n".join(self._lines)

+

+    def lines(self):

+        """The file's lines without line terminators (a copy)."""

+        return list(self._lines)

+

+    def check_position(self, line, col):

+        if line < 1 or line > len(self._lines):

+            raise SourceError("line %d out of range" % line)

+        if col < 0 or col > len(self._lines[line - 1]):

+            raise SourceError("column %d out of range" % col)

+

+    def text_before(self, line, col):

+        """All text from the start of the file up to the cursor."""

+        head = self._lines[: line - 1]

+        head.append(self._lines[line - 1][:col])

+        return "\n".join(head)

+# sith — design

+

+`python sith.py complete <file> <line> <col> [--fuzzy]` prints completions as JSON.

+Standard library only (`requirements.txt` lists no packages).

+

+## Decisions likely to change, and the module that hides each

+

+| Module | Secret (the decision it hides) |

+|---|---|

+| `sithlib/source.py` | How a file is read, decoded and split into lines, and how a (line, col) cursor is validated. |

+| `sithlib/parsing.py` | The repair strategy that turns broken source into a syntax tree without shifting line numbers. |

+| `sithlib/cursor.py` | How the text before the cursor is lexed into a context (name / attribute / none), the typed prefix, and the receiver expression. |

+| `sithlib/scopes.py` | How bindings are found in the tree, which scope owns them, and the (indentation-aware) rules for the scope at a cursor and for visibility. |

+| `sithlib/modules.py` | How an imported module is located: project source file/package first, otherwise a runtime import with side effects contained. |

+| `sithlib/introspect.py` | How live Python objects are classified and their attributes enumerated and fetched safely. |

+| `sithlib/vocabulary.py` | Where builtin names and keywords come from. |

+| `sithlib/inference.py` | How bindings and expressions map to values (module/class/function/instance), name resolution through scopes, star imports and builtins, and member enumeration. |

+| `sithlib/matching.py` | The prefix / fuzzy matching algorithm and the "text still to insert" rule. |

+| `sithlib/ranking.py` | The ordering rules (public, private, dunder, keywords; case-insensitive). |

+| `sithlib/presentation.py` | The wording of the `type` and `description` fields. |

+| `sithlib/output.py` | The wire format (compact, newline-terminated JSON). |

+| `sithlib/engine.py` | The completion policy: what each cursor context offers and how filtering, wording and ranking combine. |

+| `sith.py` | Command-line parsing, exit codes and error reporting. |

+

+## Interfaces between modules

+

+Modules talk only through small interfaces, never through each other's internal

+data structures:

+

+* `cursor.analyze(text_before) -> CursorContext(kind, prefix, receiver_text)`

+* `inference.Project(path, text).location(line, col)` returns a `Location` with

+  `visible_entities()` and `evaluate(expression_text)`.

+* A `Value` exposes `kind`, `type_name` and `members()`; an `Entity` exposes `name`,

+  `presentation() -> (kind, type_name)` and `value()`.

+* `matching.matches(name, query, fuzzy)` and `matching.remaining_text(name, query)`.

+* `ranking.rank(items, name_of, is_keyword)`.

+* `presentation.describe(name, kind, type_name) -> (type, description)`.

+* `output.write_completions([(name, complete, type, description), ...])`.

+

+## Behaviour choices where the specification is silent

+

+* Inside a comment or string literal, no completions are returned.

+* `True`, `False` and `None` are offered only as keywords, not also as builtins.

+* Class scopes are not visible from inside their methods, matching Python.

+* Literal receivers list every attribute of their builtin type, dunders included.

+  Module receivers list public names only.

+* Star imports bring in every public name. `__all__` is not consulted.

+* A trailing newline at the end of the file counts as an extra, empty last line, so

+  the cursor can sit on it.

+"""Completion ordering.

+

+Secret: the ranking rules — public names, then private, then dunder names,

+then keywords, each group alphabetical ignoring case.

+"""

+

+

+def _group(name, is_keyword):

+    if is_keyword:

+        return 3

+    if name.startswith("__") and name.endswith("__"):

+        return 2

+    if name.startswith("_"):

+        return 1

+    return 0

+

+

+def rank(items, name_of, is_keyword):

+    """Return ``items`` sorted; ``name_of``/``is_keyword`` describe an item."""

+    return sorted(items, key=lambda item: (_group(name_of(item), is_keyword(item)),

+                                           name_of(item).lower(), name_of(item)))

+"""Query matching.

+

+Secret: the algorithm deciding whether a typed query matches a candidate

+name (case-insensitive prefix, or case-insensitive in-order subsequence when

+fuzzy) and how much of the name remains to be inserted.

+"""

+

+

+def matches(name, query, fuzzy=False):

+    if not query:

+        return True

+    name, query = name.lower(), query.lower()

+    if not fuzzy:

+        return name.startswith(query)

+    position = 0

+    for ch in query:

+        position = name.find(ch, position)

+        if position < 0:

+            return False

+        position += 1

+    return True

+

+

+def remaining_text(name, query):

+    """Text to insert: the name minus as many characters as were typed."""

+    return name[len(query):]

+"""sith - static Python code completion.

+

+Usage: python sith.py complete <file> <line> <col> [--fuzzy]

+"""

+

+import os

+import sys

+

+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

+

+from sithlib import engine, output  # noqa: E402

+from sithlib.source import SourceError  # noqa: E402

+

+USAGE = "usage: sith.py complete <file> <line> <col> [--fuzzy]"

+

+

+def _fail(message):

+    sys.stderr.write("error: %s\n" % message)

+    return 1

+

+

+def main(argv):

+    sys.setrecursionlimit(max(sys.getrecursionlimit(), 10000))

+    fuzzy = "--fuzzy" in argv

+    args = [a for a in argv if a != "--fuzzy"]

+    if len(args) != 4 or args[0] != "complete":

+        return _fail(USAGE)

+    try:

+        line, col = int(args[2]), int(args[3])

+    except ValueError:

+        return _fail("line and column must be integers")

+    try:

+        completions = engine.complete(args[1], line, col, fuzzy)

+    except SourceError as exc:

+        return _fail(str(exc))

+    except Exception:  # analysis must never crash on odd input; degrade to nothing

+        completions = []

+    output.write_completions(completions)

+    return 0

+

+

+if __name__ == "__main__":

+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

+"""Runtime object introspection.

+

+Secret: how a live Python object is classified (module, class, function or

+instance) and how its attributes are enumerated and fetched safely.

+"""

+

+import inspect

+

+MODULE = "module"

+CLASS = "class"

+FUNCTION = "function"

+INSTANCE = "instance"

+

+

+def kind_of(obj):

+    if inspect.ismodule(obj):

+        return MODULE

+    if isinstance(obj, type):

+        return CLASS

+    if inspect.isroutine(obj):

+        return FUNCTION

+    return INSTANCE

+

+

+def type_name(obj):

+    """Name of the type of ``obj`` (for describing instances)."""

+    return type(obj).__name__

+

+

+def class_name(cls):

+    return getattr(cls, "__name__", type(cls).__name__)

+

+

+def attribute_names(obj):

+    try:

+        return [n for n in dir(obj) if isinstance(n, str)]

+    except Exception:

+        return []

+

+

+def get_attribute(obj, name):

+    """Return ``(True, value)`` or ``(False, None)`` if fetching fails."""

+    try:

+        return True, getattr(obj, name)

+    except BaseException:  # noqa: B902 - descriptors may raise anything

+        return False, None

+

+

+def is_data_descriptor(obj):

+    return inspect.isdatadescriptor(obj)

+

+

+_SAFE_SAMPLE_MODULES = ("builtins",)

+

+

+def sample_instance(cls):

+    """An instance of ``cls`` built without side effects, or None."""

+    if getattr(cls, "__module__", None) not in _SAFE_SAMPLE_MODULES:

+        return None

+    try:

+        return cls()

+    except BaseException:  # noqa: B902 - constructors may raise anything

+        return None

+"""Completion engine.

+

+Secret: the completion policy — which candidates each cursor context offers

+(visible names plus keywords, or public module members, or receiver

+attributes) and how filtering, wording and ranking are combined.

+"""

+

+from . import cursor, matching, presentation, ranking, vocabulary

+from .inference import MODULE, Project

+from .source import SourceFile

+

+

+def complete(path, line, col, fuzzy=False):

+    """Return completions as a list of (name, complete, type, description)."""

+    source = SourceFile(path)

+    source.check_position(line, col)

+    context = cursor.analyze(source.text_before(line, col))

+    if context.kind == cursor.NONE:

+        return []

+

+    location = Project(source.path, source.text()).location(line, col)

+    keywords = []

+    if context.kind == cursor.NAME:

+        entities = location.visible_entities()

+        keywords = vocabulary.keywords()

+    else:

+        receiver = location.evaluate(context.receiver)

+        entities = receiver.members()

+        if receiver.kind == MODULE:

+            entities = {n: e for n, e in entities.items() if not n.startswith("_")}

+

+    query = context.prefix

+    results = []

+    for name, entity in entities.items():

+        if matching.matches(name, query, fuzzy):

+            kind, type_name = entity.presentation()

+            results.append((name, False) + presentation.describe(name, kind, type_name))

+    for word in keywords:

+        if word not in entities and matching.matches(word, query, fuzzy):

+            results.append((word, True) + presentation.describe(word, presentation.KEYWORD))

+

+    ordered = ranking.rank(results, name_of=lambda r: r[0], is_keyword=lambda r: r[1])

+    return [(name, matching.remaining_text(name, query), kind, description)

+            for name, _, kind, description in ordered]
